panels.title: Live positions
panels.description: Most recent reading per vehicle, device clock ordered. A vehicle that is offline stays at its last known position until its backlog arrives.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (vehicle_id)
  vehicle_id,
  lat AS latitude,
  lon AS longitude,
  speed_kph,
  battery_pct
FROM telemetry
WHERE device_ts > now() - interval '15 minutes'
ORDER BY vehicle_id, device_ts DESC

panels.title: Fleet status
panels.description: Driven by MQTT connect and last-will messages, not by polling. A vehicle goes offline within about a second of losing its connection.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  v.id AS "Vehicle",
  CASE WHEN s.online THEN 'online' ELSE 'OFFLINE' END AS "State",
  round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - s.last_seen))::numeric) AS "Silent (s)"
FROM vehicle v
LEFT JOIN vehicle_status s ON s.vehicle_id = v.id
ORDER BY s.online ASC, v.id

panels.title: Readings per minute — by device clock vs by arrival
panels.description: The same data bucketed two ways. Device clock stays near the true sample rate because replayed readings fill in retroactively. Arrival drops to zero during an outage and spikes when the backlog lands.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  time_bucket('1 minute', device_ts) AS time,
  count(*) AS "by device clock"
FROM telemetry
WHERE $__timeFilter(device_ts)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

SELECT
  time_bucket('1 minute', received_at) AS time,
  count(*) AS "by arrival"
FROM telemetry
WHERE $__timeFilter(received_at)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Delivery lag percentiles
panels.description: received_at minus device_ts. p50 is the steady state. p99 spikes to the length of an outage when a buffered backlog is replayed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  time_bucket('1 minute', received_at) AS time,
  percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (received_at - device_ts))) AS p50,
  percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (received_at - device_ts))) AS p95,
  percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (received_at - device_ts))) AS p99
FROM telemetry
WHERE $__timeFilter(received_at)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time
SELECT count(*) AS value FROM telemetry WHERE $__timeFilter(device_ts)

panels.title: Missed-tick gaps
panels.description: Intervals longer than two seconds between consecutive readings, device clock ordered. Zero means every second of the journey was recovered despite the outages.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS value FROM (
  SELECT device_ts - lag(device_ts) OVER (PARTITION BY vehicle_id ORDER BY device_ts) AS d
  FROM telemetry
  WHERE $__timeFilter(device_ts)
) g WHERE d > interval '2 seconds'

panels.title: Duplicate rows
panels.description: Rows sharing a (vehicle_id, device_ts) key. Always zero: redelivered readings hit ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and are discarded by the database, not by application code.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS value FROM (
  SELECT vehicle_id, device_ts
  FROM telemetry
  WHERE $__timeFilter(device_ts)
  GROUP BY 1, 2
  HAVING count(*) > 1
) d

panels.title: Worst delivery lag
panels.description: Oldest reading in a replayed backlog. Bounded by outage length, which is what proves the buffer is not leaking.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(max(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (received_at - device_ts))), 0) AS value
FROM telemetry
WHERE $__timeFilter(device_ts)
